# Changelog

What changed in OpenBGA QM LIMS, newest first: grouped by month, then ranked by impact. The application shows the same list under **What's new**. Each change is a file in [changelog.d/](changelog.d/); entry types follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). The project is pre-1.0 and does not yet promise a stable interface.

## November 2026 (2026-11-10 to 2026-11-19)

### High impact

- **Added**: Plan open tests on a work list and see reminders of what falls due · Planning · 2026-11-19 · [#61](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/61)

  A new **Planning** section lists every test that is open or awaiting review, earliest due first, with the analyst it is assigned to and the instrument it is planned on. A test is due by the date a reviewer or quality person sets, or by the **turnaround target** quality sets for lot, stability or reassessment testing; a test keeps the target in force when it was assigned. Reviewers and quality tick tests and use **Plan selected tests** to give them a due date, an analyst and an instrument at once; an analyst can **Assign to me** a test nobody has taken. **Workload** shows open work by due date, by analyst and by instrument, and flags an instrument whose calibration runs out before its planned work. **Reminders** lists the calibrations, stability pulls and reagent and standard lots that fall due in the coming days, and the dashboard counts the tests overdue. Planning authorizes nothing: recording a result still checks the analyst's qualification, the instrument and every lot.

  In the application: **Work list**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - New app `planning` with migrations `planning.0001_initial` (`Target`, `Plan`) and `planning.0002_planning_guards`: targets are append-only by trigger; a plan is never deleted, stays with its test, advances its revision on every change and is written only while its test is open or awaiting review.
  > - Pages `planning:work_list`, `planning:plan`, `planning:workload`, `planning:reminders`, `planning:targets` and `planning:targets_change`; the POST-only action `planning:take`. New remote lookups `analysts` and `instruments-in-service`. Audit actions `plan.changed`, `plan.taken` and `turnaround_target.set`.
  > - No target exists after the upgrade, so open tests have no due date until quality sets targets (which apply to tests assigned afterwards) or a planner sets dates.
  > - Reminders are computed when the page is opened; nothing is sent and no scheduled job is added.

- **Added**: Record training, qualify people to review a method, and see qualifications falling due · Laboratory · 2026-11-19

  **Laboratory** has a new **Training** tab. Someone other than the trainee records a person's training in a method or activity, and the trainee confirms it with **Acknowledge** and their signature. A qualification now states whether it is for **Performing the work** or **Reviewing results**, and can rely on the person's acknowledged **Training records**. A method version can ask for **Reviewers qualified for the method**. A result of that version is then reviewed or returned only by a reviewer who holds a current qualification to review the method, and the test shows which qualification the review relied on. **Planning > Reminders** also lists qualifications that reach their last valid day with no approved renewal.

  In the application: **Training**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migrations `laboratory.0006` (the `TrainingRecord` table with a guard trigger that allows only the trainee's acknowledgement and no deletion, plus the `Qualification.work` and `Qualification.training` columns), `catalog.0008` (`MethodRevision.requires_review_qualification`) and `analytical.0013` (`AnalyticalTest.review_evidence`, and a replaced test guard that lets that column change only from awaiting review to reviewed). Existing qualifications become qualifications to perform. Existing method versions ask for no qualified reviewer, so reviews work as before until a new version is approved with the setting.
  > - New pages `laboratory:training_list`, `laboratory:training_new`, `laboratory:training_detail` and `laboratory:training_acknowledge`, and the lookup `training-records`. New audit action `training.recorded`. The acknowledgement is signed with the meaning `acknowledged`.
  > - New setting `ANALYTICAL_REVIEWERS` (default `config.integrations.LaboratoryReviewers`). A settings module without it fails the new system check `analytical.E001`. `core.services.sign_transition` now also accepts a tuple of roles as `permission`.
  > - A method version's approved content (`oq.method/1`) now carries `requires_review_qualification`. Requirement payloads frozen on tests are unchanged.

- **Added**: See turnaround and right-first-time figures of the tests reviewed in a period · Planning · 2026-11-19 · [#62](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/62)

  **Planning** has two new tabs for reviewers, quality, auditors and admins. **Figures** shows, for the tests reviewed in a period you choose, the median turnaround from assignment to review, the turnaround nine in ten tests met, how many were reviewed on time against their due date, and how many were right first time: never returned for correction, with no corrected reading, and neither a repeat nor repeated. It also counts results out of specification and those invalidated after an investigation. Choose **Figures by** to break the figures down by kind of work, material, method, analyst or month. Every count opens **Reviewed tests**, which lists those tests with their turnaround, due date and what kept each from being right first time, and can be exported with **Export filtered CSV**.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Pages `planning:figures` and `planning:reviewed` (`?export=csv` streams the filtered list as CSV). Both are read-only and need the reviewer, quality, auditor or admin role; an analyst without one of those roles receives 403 and does not see the tabs.
  > - No migration and no new table: the figures are computed when the page is opened from the review signatures (meaning `reviewed`), the `test.returned` audit events, corrected observations, the lineage of retests, resamples, reruns and repeats, and the due dates of the work list. A period is at most 366 days and dates are local days of `TIME_ZONE`.

- **Added**: Check whether a certificate someone holds was issued here and is still current · Certificates · 2026-11-18 · [#57](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/57)

  **Check a certificate** on the certificate list compares a certificate file, or its SHA-256, with every version issued and answers whether it is genuine and current, replaced by a later version, or withdrawn. The file is never kept. A laboratory can also let its customers make the same check without an account, at an address it gives them. Each check that found a certificate is listed under **Checks** on its page, which warns when a recipient still checks a withdrawn certificate.

  In the application: **Check a certificate**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migration `reporting.0006_certificate_checks`: append-only `CertificateCheck` (its insert trigger refuses an answer the certificate does not give), the one-row `CheckWindow`, and indexes on `ReportVersion.pdf_sha256` and `data_sha256`.
  > - New page `reports/check/` (URL name `reporting:check`, every reading role, in the form dialog) and, only with `CERTIFICATE_CHECK=true`, `check/` (URL name `certificate_check`) without an account, linked from the sign-in page. Off by default; it starts no session and sends `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.
  > - `CERTIFICATE_CHECK_RATE` (default 20, 1 to 600) bounds checks without an account per minute for the whole deployment, before the request body is read; past it the page answers 429 with `Retry-After`. Keep per-address rate limiting at the reverse proxy.
  > - Uploads are hashed as they arrive and never stored, within `RAW_DATA_MAX_BYTES`. Checks without an account are kept once a day for each version and answer, and a cross-site POST is refused with 403 before it is counted. The lot record export adds the section `report_checks`. The certificate prints nothing new.

- **Added**: Import results from an instrument's export file · Testing · 2026-11-18 · [#58](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/58)

  Quality can give a draft method version a **File import** that states how its instrument's export is read: the file's format, the column naming the test and the column of each input. It is approved with the version. On a test of that version, **Import results** attaches the export to the test's raw data and shows the values read from it for checking, with a field for anything the file does not hold. **Record imported results** then records every row as a replicate, with the file and the row it came from. A cell that is not a plain number refuses the whole file. Submission and review read the stored file again.

  In the application: **Specifications and methods: Methods**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migrations `catalog.0007_file_import` (the method version's `file_import`, changed on a draft like the calculation; the revision guard leaves it out of its comparison) and `analytical.0011_imported_observations` (`Observation.source_file` and `source`; a check constraint ties them together and an insert trigger requires a file of the same test).
  > - The file import is frozen in the method's approved content and in new test requirements as `oq.test-requirement/4` (the `/3` keys with an eight-key method whose `file_import` follows `oq.file-import/1`). Methods without one keep their earlier payloads and hashes.
  > - Delimited text only: comma, semicolon or tab; point or comma decimal; UTF-8, UTF-16 or Windows-1252; at most 100,000 rows of 500 columns, within `RAW_DATA_MAX_BYTES`. An export that cannot be imported is refused before it is stored.
  > - New pages `catalog:file_import_set`, `catalog:file_import_clear`, `analytical:import_new` and `analytical:import_file`; audit actions `method_revision.file_import_set`, `method_revision.file_import_cleared` and `observation.imported`.

- **Added**: Issue a certificate for a customer or a market of the lot, with each result judged against every specification · Certificates · 2026-11-18 · [#55](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/55)

  For a lot under more than one specification, such as the general one and a customer's, the certificate now states for every result whether it conforms to each specification that states the test, including one the lot was not tested against, and says how conformity is judged. On **Review certificate**, **Certificate for** lets quality issue a certificate for one customer or market of the lot instead: it lists the tests that specification states, with its limits, names no other customer or market, and is refused while a result does not meet them. The certificate list, record and versions show the scope, and each method is now listed once on a certificate.

  In the application: **Certificates of analysis**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migration `reporting.0004_certificate_scope`: `Report.scope` (blank for all of the lot's requirements) and a replaced head guard: the scope is fixed once a version is issued, and only a record opened but never issued takes another scope (audit action `report.scope_changed`). A recipient's issued certificate is amended, or withdrawn before a certificate for another scope is issued to the same recipient. Reversing the migration restores the guard of `reporting.0003`.
  > - The certificate evidence of a lot whose frozen requirements name more than one specification gains `native.conformity` (each reportable result and accepted supplier result with one statement per specification: `conforms`, `does_not_conform`, `not_judged` with a reason, `information` or `not_tested`); the issued snapshot keeps the scope under `report.scope`. Evidence of a lot under one specification is unchanged.
  > - The judgement uses the testing rules on the recorded readings, with no conversion of unit, result type, outcome criterion, replicate count, method or retest allowance, and no measurement uncertainty (simple acceptance).

- **Added**: Read values from balances and meters connected to the analyst's computer · Testing · 2026-11-18 · [#59](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/59)

  Quality can give a balance or meter a **data connection** on its equipment record (**More**, **Set data connection**): the format it answers in, its serial settings and the serial number it reports. METTLER TOLEDO balances (MT-SICS), A&D balances (A&D standard format) and Orion Star A-series meters are supported. On **Record observation** and **Correct observation**, in Chrome or Edge, **Read from** fills a value with the instrument's reading. A weight the balance did not report as stable, another unit or another device is refused. Every reading is kept on the test as the device sent it, whether or not a replicate records it, and the test record and the review show which values were read and which were typed.

  In the application: **Equipment**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migrations `laboratory.0005_device_connections` (`DeviceConnection`, append-only by trigger: only its end is set, once; one current connection per equipment) and `analytical.0012_instrument_readings` (`InstrumentReading`; a trigger refuses deletes and any change except linking a reading once to an observation of the same test recorded by the reader).
  > - The browser uses the Web Serial API, which needs a secure context (HTTPS, or `localhost`). The application sends no `Permissions-Policy` header; a proxy that adds `serial=()` turns readings off. Without the API values are typed.
  > - The device's answer is read on the server (`core/device_formats.py`); the browser passes it on base64-encoded to the POST-only JSON endpoint `analytical:instrument_read` and never sends a value.
  > - New pages `laboratory:equipment_connection_new` and `laboratory:equipment_connection_end`; audit actions `equipment.connection_set`, `equipment.connection_ended` and `instrument.read`; `observation.recorded` and `observation.corrected` list the readings they record. The lot record export adds the section `instrument_readings`.
  > - The formats were built from the manufacturers' published interface descriptions and tested with simulated devices. Verify each connection with the laboratory's own instrument before relying on it.

- **Added**: Acceptance journeys run passing, failing, corrected, rejected and amended records end to end · Deployment · 2026-11-17 · [#49](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/49)

  A deployment can run five record journeys (passing, failing, corrected, rejected and amended) with the release it is about to use, in a new database of its own environment. Each step records what was expected and what happened, including the refusals, and the run keeps a report, each lot's record export and the certificates with their checksums as evidence for the laboratory's own acceptance. The journeys use synthetic configuration, not the laboratory's.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > Acceptance journeys: `python manage.py acceptance_journeys --database NAME --output DIR --operator NAME` runs five journeys (passing, failing, corrected, rejected and amended records) end to end through the application's services in a new database migrated to the release, refusing a database other than the one named, one that holds any account or one not migrated to exactly this release. Each step records what was expected and observed and the product requirements it gives evidence for, including refusals (self-review, a wrong PIN counted and audited, disposition or rejection by an author, release while an investigation is open, a second retest, invalidation by a failing retest, requirements, a disposition or a certificate for a rejected lot, a stale amendment, and direct database changes to a certificate, an observation, a signature and an audit event). The evidence folder holds `report.html`, `report.json` (`oq.acceptance-journeys/1`), each lot's record export, the certificates and `SHA256SUMS`; the command exits nonzero when a step failed. Guidance in `docs/operations.md` ("Acceptance journeys").

- **Added**: Assess the impact of a failure on tests, lots, stability studies and certificates · Impact assessments · 2026-11-17 · [#54](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/54)

  When equipment, a reagent or standard, a supplier, a contract laboratory or anything else fails, a quality person starts an assessment under **Impact assessments**, or with **Assess impact** on the page of the record that failed, for the period the problem may have affected. The system lists the tests, lots, stability studies and certificates it can find from the cause; quality adds any other, records for each whether it was **Affected** and what is done about it, and can **Place hold** on an affected lot. A quality person who took no part in it concludes the assessment with a signature, and the lot record and the dashboard show the assessments open.

  In the application: **Impact assessments**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - New app `impact` with migrations `impact.0001_initial` and `impact.0002_impact_guards` (the `Assessment` and `Item` tables and their database guards).
  > - Audit actions `impact.started`, `impact.records_found`, `impact.record_added`, `impact.record_decided` and `impact.hold_placed`; signature meanings `impact_assessed` and `withdrawn` on `impact.assessment`. The conclusion freezes `oq.impact-assessment/1`.
  > - A hold placed through an assessment is an ordinary `stability.Hold` of kind `quality` whose reference names the assessment. New remote lookups `equipment`, `reagent-lots` and `contract-laboratories`.
  > - The lot record export gains the section `impact_records` (the lot's records in assessments, not the assessments, which name other lots); the dashboard gains the queue **Impact assessments open**.

- **Added**: Cancel a lot received in error with a signed record · Lots · 2026-11-17 · [#44](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/44)

  **Cancel lot received in error** records, with a signature, that a lot should not have been received. It is refused once the lot has a sample, test, reserve sample, stability study or standing supplier result.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Signed cancellation of a lot received in error (`quality:lot_cancel`, **Cancel lot received in error**): meaning `cancelled`, evidence `oq.lot-cancellation/1`; refused once the lot has a sample, test, reserve sample, stability study or standing supplier result, and signed by someone other than whoever received the lot or made its records.

- **Changed**: Every form opens in a dialog over the record, signing included · Whole application · 2026-11-17

  Adding a sample, recording a pull or a result, correcting a receipt, creating an account and every other form now opens in a dialog over the page it was opened from, with the page dimmed behind it. Signing forms open the same way on the signature card: the signing username and PIN are entered every time, a refused PIN is cleared, and nothing about who may sign or what a signature binds has changed. **Signature PIN** shows its state, and **Change signature PIN** opens the change in a dialog. Security keys and passkeys register inside the dialog too. Opening a form's address directly shows it over its record or list, and every signature asks for the reason, then the signing username and PIN, in that order.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - `core/form_surfaces.py` registers every form route with its dialog size and roles; `tests/test_form_dialog.py` fails when a form route is neither registered nor listed as a page with its reason (the two sign-in steps, the two-factor overview and a required password change, which has no Cancel).
  > - Signing in the dialog keeps the server checks: a refused PIN answers 422 with the PIN cleared and the attempt counted, a stale revision is refused, and success answers 204 with `HX-Redirect` to the record.
  > - New URL names `core:pin_status` (`/signature-pin/`); the change form `core:pin` moved to `/signature-pin/change/`.
  > - Every date-time field uses the shared date-time control at minute precision.

- **Changed**: New visual design for the whole interface · Whole application · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  The interface has a new look, **Line**: calm tonal surfaces, rounded panels, a petrol accent and one type family, in light and dark. Each record answers what matters now first, with status and hold pills, the critical facts and the actions that resolve a state beside one primary action. Scientific, signing and audit behaviour is unchanged.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Every template of every app is built on one component registry (`{% load ui %}`, `core/templatetags/ui.py`): isolated, keyword-only tags for panels, notices, lists, facts, record layouts, form pages, form dialogs, signature cards, history, status pills, material tags and code chips. Per-app copies of empty states, pagers, history and toolbars are gone; `tests/test_include_isolation.py` and `tests/test_ui_standards.py` enforce it.
  > - Design tokens have full scales (space, type, weight, radius, shadow, z-index) with `--bs-*` semantic colours mapped onto them for light, dark and print; no colour literals outside the Tokens section (`tests/test_css_tokens.py`). Bootstrap Icons only, copied verbatim (`tests/test_icons.py`).
  > - Records lead with status and hold pills, the material tag and the critical facts (holds, out-of-specification results, overdue, revoked, amended, superseded). The lot record and signing share one `disposition_blockers()` list, extracted from `dispose_lot` with the same order and conditions under the lock. The signature dialog markup moved to `{% signature_card %}` with unchanged semantics.
  > - Tests changed on evidence: markup assertions moved to stable hooks (`data-audit-action`, `data-signature-dialog`, and similar); none was weakened. The page documentation, the roadmap and `docs/product.md` status were updated with the change.

- **Added**: Reassess released material whose retest date is near, for a later retest date or the end of its use · Lots · 2026-11-17 · [#53](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/53)

  An analyst or quality person starts a reassessment of a released lot from its **Reassessments** panel, with the sample taken for it; its tests come from the specifications in force and leave the lot's original record as signed. Once the results are reviewed, a quality person who did none of the work signs **Suitable** with a new retest date, never after the expiry date, or **Not suitable**, after which the lot shows **Use ended** and takes no certificate. The new retest date appears on the lot record, in **Material lots** and on the certificate of analysis, and the dashboard counts lots due for retest and reassessments open.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migrations `quality.0014_reassessment` (the `Reassessment` table and its database guards) and `analytical.0010_reassessment_tests` (a test may belong to a reassessment; the subject constraint is now `analytical_test_subject_of_three`).
  > - New setting `ANALYTICAL_REASSESSMENTS` (default `config.integrations.Reassessments`). Audit action `lot.reassessment_started`; signature meanings `reassessed` and `withdrawn` on `quality.reassessment`. The conclusion freezes `oq.reassessment-results/1`.
  > - The certificate evidence's `dates` gains `reassessment` or `use_ended` only for a lot that has one. The lot record export gains the sections `reassessments` and `reassessment_tests`.
  > - The dashboard's **Certificates to issue** queue now leaves out released lots that cannot take a certificate: expired, due for retest or whose use ended.

- **Added**: Record a lot's expiry and retest dates, checked at release and printed on the certificate · Lots · 2026-11-17

  An analyst or quality person records a lot's **Expiry date** and **Retest date** with their basis from the lot record while it is in quarantine; a correction keeps the record it replaces, and whoever recorded them cannot sign the lot's disposition. The release is refused after the expiry date and from the retest date on, and when a date the rule set requires is missing. The certificate of analysis prints the dates, released lots show **Retest due** or **Expired**, and **Material lots** can list lots by their dates.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migration `quality.0013_lot_dates` adds the append-only `LotDates` table with its database guards. Audit actions `lot.dates_recorded` and `lot.dates_corrected`.
  > - A rule policy may carry `material_dates` (`expiry`, `retest`, `expiry_or_retest` or `expiry_and_retest`); rule sets without it require no dates.
  > - For a lot with dates, the release's `disposition_evidence`, the rejection and cancellation evidence and the certificate evidence gain a `dates` key; other lots keep their evidence shape. Certificates are not issued or amended for a lot that has expired or whose retest date has been reached.

- **Added**: Record and accept the system's intended use · Validation · 2026-11-17 · [#43](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/43)

  Under **Validation**, quality records what the system is used for and what is outside it, and a different quality person accepts it with a signature. The acceptance freezes the approved versions in force and the running release, and the list shows what changed since.

  In the application: **Intended use**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Validation records of the laboratory, under the new sidebar item **Validation** (app `validation`). **Intended use** (`validation:use_list`, `use_new`, `use_detail`, `use_accept`, `use_withdraw`): quality records what the system is used for and what is outside it, the supported assays (methods with an approved version in force), the process owner and the system owner, other responsibilities, the validation report and the known issues and conditions; a different quality person accepts it with a signature that freezes every approved rule set, specification, method, sampling plan and stability protocol version in force and the running release (`SOURCE_REVISION` or `RENDER_GIT_COMMIT`), and supersedes the previous acceptance. The list and the accepted record show what changed since.
  > - New tables `validation.UseAcceptance`, `validation.Rehearsal` and `validation.RehearsalFile` (migrations `validation.0001_initial` and `validation.0002_guards`, whose triggers keep recorded content immutable, allow only the signed or withdrawn transitions and keep evidence files append-only).
  > - New audit actions `use_acceptance.recorded`, `use_acceptance.superseded`, `use_acceptance.withdrawn`, `rehearsal.recorded`, `rehearsal.file_attached` and `rehearsal.withdrawn`; the acceptances are `signed.accepted`.

- **Added**: Record rehearsals of recovery, downtime and upgrade · Validation · 2026-11-17 · [#43](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/43)

  Quality or an administrator records a rehearsal of recovery from backup, downtime and reconciliation, or an upgrade, and attaches its evidence files. A quality person who did not record it accepts it.

  In the application: **Rehearsals**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - **Rehearsals** (`validation:rehearsal_list`, `rehearsal_new`, `rehearsal_detail`, `rehearsal_file_new`, `rehearsal_file`, `rehearsal_accept`, `rehearsal_withdraw`): quality or admin records a rehearsal of recovery from backup, downtime and reconciliation, or an upgrade, the recorder attaches its evidence files, and a quality person who did not record it accepts it. Guidance in `docs/operations.md` ("Validation records of the laboratory").
  > - The restore check's `raw data files` check also verifies rehearsal evidence files, and its summary counts both. `RAW_DATA_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES` is one ceiling for raw-data files and rehearsal evidence together, for both kinds of upload (`core.uploads.stored_bytes`); the refusal now reads "This deployment has reached its storage limit for files."

- **Added**: Record that a test cannot be completed, with its repeat or investigation · Testing · 2026-11-17 · [#45](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/45)

  **Record not completed** on an open test lets a quality person who is not one of the test's data authors give the cause and a reason and sign. The test keeps everything recorded on it and is repeated or investigated, and the test list has a **Not completed** status filter.

  In the application: **Testing: tests**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Signed record that a test cannot be completed (`analytical:test_not_completed`, **Record not completed** on an open test, quality role, not the test's data authors): the cause (sample lost, damaged or used up; an error in preparing or running the test; equipment, reagent or standard failure; another cause) and a reason, signed with the meaning `not_completed`; the test keeps everything recorded on it and its new state `not_completed` holds `not_completed_record` (`oq.test-not-completed/1`). A test of an investigation is left to it; readings outside the limits open an investigation on the test; any other test is repeated by a linked test of the new kind `repeat`, on the same sample, the pulled material of a stability pull or a new sample of the lot that stands in for it. The test list has a **Not completed** status filter.
  > - New migration `analytical.0009_not_completed_tests`: `AnalyticalTest.not_completed_record`, the state `not_completed`, the kind `repeat` (allowed without an investigation and on a stability pull), a check constraint keeping the record present exactly in that state, and a test guard that lets only an open test move to it and keeps it immutable afterwards. `lot_evidence` lists such tests under `excluded_tests` with a `not_completed` entry (cause, follow-up, signature); a pull's frozen results list them under `excluded_tests`.
  > - A test recorded as not completed does not fix its QC batch's results and is left as it is when the batch is rejected; the replacement of a lot's requirements treats it as closed. The refusals of a lot rejection and of a requirement replacement for unsubmitted readings now name this record as the alternative to submitting.

- **Added**: Reject a lot in quarantine with a signed record · Lots · 2026-11-17 · [#44](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/44)

  On the lot record, **Reject lot** lets a quality person outside the lot's authors choose the grounds, state the reason and sign. The signature freezes what stood in the way of release, and rejection is refused while an investigation is open or a result outside its limits was not submitted.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Signed rejection of a lot in quarantine (`quality:lot_reject`, **Reject lot** on the lot record): a quality person outside the lot's authors chooses the grounds, states the reason and may name the quality system's record; the signature (meaning `rejected`) freezes, as `oq.lot-rejection/1` in `Lot.disposition_evidence`, what stood in the way of release, the lot's tests, investigations, receipt, supplier certificates and results and active holds. Refused while an investigation is open or a test holds a recorded result outside its limits that was not submitted.
  > - `Lot.state` takes the choices `quarantine`, `released`, `rejected` and `cancelled` under a check constraint, and the lot guard (migration `quality.0012_lot_rejection`) refuses every change of a lot that left quarantine, not only of a released one; a rejected or cancelled lot's evidence must name its `decision` and `schema`, and a released lot's never does.
  > - Rejecting a failed QC batch leaves the tests of a rejected lot as they are (no invalidation, no rerun) instead of refusing the whole batch.

- **Added**: Withdraw an issued certificate with a signature and record that its recipients were notified · Certificates · 2026-11-17 · [#54](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/54)

  A quality person withdraws a certificate of analysis that can no longer be relied on with **Withdraw certificate** under **More** on its page, stating why and, optionally, the impact assessment or quality-system record behind it. The certificate then shows **Withdrawn** and takes no amendment; every issued version and its PDF stay exactly as issued, and a later certificate for the lot is a new numbered one. **Record notification** keeps who was told, when, how and where the evidence is kept; the certificate list filters **Withdrawn** and **Awaiting notification**, and the dashboard counts withdrawn certificates whose recipients are not yet recorded as notified.

  In the application: **Certificates of analysis**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migration `reporting.0003_certificate_withdrawal`: `Report.withdrawn_at`, `withdrawal_reason` and `withdrawal_reference`, the state `withdrawn`, the partial unique constraint `report_lot_recipient_current` in place of `report_lot_recipient`, the `RecipientNotification` table, a replaced head guard and an append-only guard on notifications. Reversing it is refused while a withdrawn certificate exists.
  > - Signature meaning `withdrawn` on `reporting.report`; audit action `report.recipient_notified`. The lot record export gains the section `report_notifications`.
  > - The dashboard's **Certificates to issue** counts a released lot again once all its certificates are withdrawn.

- **Security**: A stopped second factor stays stopped when a new app is confirmed · Account access · 2026-11-16 · [#36](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/36)

  After 100 wrong codes stop two-factor sign-in, confirming a new authenticator app no longer clears the stop. Only an administrator's reset does.

  In the application: **Two-factor sign-in**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Confirming a new authenticator app after 100 wrong codes stopped two-factor sign-in no longer clears the stop; a setup started before the stop is refused, and only an administrator's reset clears it.

- **Added**: Backup manifests and restore checks kept as evidence · Deployment · 2026-11-16 · [#31](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/31)

  Two commands let an operator record what a backup should contain and check a restored copy against it. The report can be kept as evidence of the restore, and the application image includes the PostgreSQL client tools.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Backup and restore checks. `python manage.py backup_manifest --output FILE [--dump ARCHIVE]` reads the database in one read-only snapshot and writes a manifest: each table's row count and SHA-256 fingerprint, the columns, constraints, indexes, triggers and functions, the applied migrations and the sequence positions, and checks of the stored evidence (signature hashes and their audit events, issued certificate and raw-data checksums, enabled triggers). With `--dump` it runs `pg_dump` from the same snapshot and records the archive's checksum. `python manage.py verify_restore --manifest FILE --report FILE [--archive ARCHIVE]` checks a restored copy against the manifest and writes a report to keep as evidence; it fails unless the copy equals the manifest and its evidence is intact, and refuses the source database as a copy. Both commands only read, never overwrite a file and write files readable by their owner only.
  > - The application image includes the PostgreSQL 17 client tools (`pg_dump`, `pg_restore`, `psql`), and the container smoke job backs up, restores and checks a seeded copy with the image.

- **Security**: Django admin sign-in goes through the application's sign-in · Sign-in · 2026-11-16 · [#34](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/34)

  The sign-in page of Django admin no longer signs anyone in. It sends the person to the application's sign-in, so the sign-in lock and the two-factor step apply to every session.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Django admin's own sign-in page (`/admin/login/`) no longer signs anyone in: it redirects to the application's sign-in, with the admin page to return to, so the sign-in lock and the two-factor step apply to every session.

- **Added**: Export a lot's complete record as one package · Lots · 2026-11-16 · [#33](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/33)

  **Export record** on the lot page downloads one ZIP file with a printed copy, an electronic copy, the lot's raw-data files and issued certificates byte for byte, and a checksum list. It is available to the admin, quality and auditor roles, and the export is recorded in the lot's audit trail.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Export of a lot's complete record: **Export record** on the lot page (admin, quality and auditor, the roles that read the audit trail) downloads one ZIP file with a printed copy (`record.pdf`), an electronic copy (`record.json`, schema `oq.lot-record/1`, every stored field with its label, kind and choices), the lot's raw-data files and issued certificates byte for byte, `manifest.json` and a `SHA256SUMS` list. Everything is read in one repeatable-read, read-only transaction. It covers the lot's receipt details, supplier certificates and accepted supplier results, requirement assignments, samples and sampling records, tests and the tests of its stability pulls, observations, raw-data files, investigations, QC batches, certificates, stability studies, reserves, retention obligations and holds, the instruments, reagent lots and contract laboratory reports used, the configuration they name (including the specification, method and rule set versions frozen in its requirements), every signature with its manifestation, the audit trail and its reviews. The checksums of stored files and the hashes stored with signatures, certificates, requirement assignments and approved versions are recomputed and each outcome is stated. The export states its purpose and is recorded in the lot's audit trail (`lot.record_exported`) with the package's SHA-256; nothing else changes.

- **Added**: Require two-factor sign-in for chosen roles · Account access · 2026-11-16 · [#34](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/34)

  A deployment can require two-factor sign-in for chosen roles or for everyone. Until it is set up, such an account reaches only the two-factor page, password change, page help and sign-out.

  In the application: **Two-factor sign-in**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - The new setting `MFA_REQUIRED_ROLES` (comma-separated laboratory roles or `all`; empty by default) requires it: such an account reaches only the two-factor page, password change, page help and sign-out until it is set up. Shared demonstration accounts cannot set it up and are never required to.

- **Added**: Security keys and passkeys as a second sign-in factor · Account access · 2026-11-16 · [#36](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/36)

  On **Two-factor sign-in** an owner can add a named security key or passkey and use it at the second sign-in step beside, or instead of, a code from an app. Keys work only at the host name they were registered at, over HTTPS or on `localhost`.

  In the application: **Two-factor sign-in**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Security keys and passkeys (Web Authentication) as a second sign-in factor. On **Two-factor sign-in** an owner adds a named key (**Add a security key or passkey**, page `/accounts/two-factor/security-key/`) after confirming the password, and a second factor once two-factor sign-in is on; the first key turns it on and shows ten recovery codes. The second sign-in step offers **Use your security key** beside the code field, and every owner change can be confirmed with a key by leaving the code empty. A refused key counts like a wrong code toward the sign-in lock and the 100-failure stop; each challenge is answered once; a signature count that does not increase is refused and logged. Keys can be removed one by one (the last one turns two-factor sign-in off, refused for a required role), and **Remove the authenticator app** keeps the keys. The administrator reset removes keys too. Keys work only at the host name they were registered at, over HTTPS or on `localhost`. New audit actions `account.security_key_added`, `account.security_key_removed`, `account.authenticator_added` and `account.authenticator_removed`.
  > - Security keys and passkeys: `sign_in_factors` can be `["password", "security_key"]`; account audit values gain `authenticator_app` and `security_keys` (a count). New table `accounts.SecurityKey` (migration `accounts.0008_security_keys`): public key, credential ID, signature count, host name (`rp_id`) and the owner's name for each key; no secret. New dependency `webauthn` (py_webauthn), which installs `cryptography`, `pyOpenSSL`, `cbor2`, `pyasn1` and `pyasn1-modules`. Two-factor sign-in's start buttons are now **Set up with a security key or passkey** and **Set up with an authenticator app**; for an account without an app the second step's field is labelled **Recovery code**.

- **Added**: Sign in with a passkey alone, without the password · Sign-in · 2026-11-16 · [#37](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/37)

  **Sign in** offers **Sign in with a passkey** for a key that checks its holder's PIN, fingerprint or face. A deployment that prefers the password first can turn it off.

  In the application: **Two-factor sign-in**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Signing in with a security key or passkey alone, without the password. **Sign in** offers **Sign in with a passkey** (when the site is opened by its host name), which opens `/accounts/login/passkey/`: **Use your passkey** asks the browser for a key the person added on **Two-factor sign-in**, with no account named, and the key must check its holder's PIN, fingerprint or face. The key's credential identifies the account and the answer must carry its user handle. Refused answers are logged and not counted (a signature cannot be guessed, and counting would let anyone who has seen a credential ID lock the account); an account that is locked or stopped refuses even a valid key. A request is answered once within five minutes. A key that does not check its holder still works after the password. The PIN is still re-entered for every signature.
  > - Signing in with a key alone: `sign_in_factors` can be `["passkey"]`. The new setting `PASSKEY_SIGN_IN` (default `true`) offers it; set it to `false` to ask every account for its password first. `accounts.security_keys.verify_assertion` takes the purpose `passkey`, for which the ceremony names no account, and then requires the user handle and user verification. When a key cannot be used, the message of `static/js/security-keys.js` ends with the form's `data-security-key-fallback` (default "use a code"). The sign-in log gains `signin.passkey_failed`.

- **Added**: Single sign-on with the organization's identity provider · Account access · 2026-11-16 · [#40](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/40)

  Where the deployment sets it up, an owner links their account to the organization's identity provider on **Organization sign-in** and then uses **Sign in with** that provider on the sign-in page. Administrators can remove a link with a signed action.

  In the application: **Organization sign-in**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Single sign-on with the organization's identity provider (OpenID Connect authorization code flow with PKCE), off unless `OIDC_ISSUER`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` and `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` are set; also `OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME`, `OIDC_SCOPES`, `OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD` and `OIDC_PROMPT` (default `login`). Owners link their own account on the new page **Organization sign-in** (`accounts:single_sign_on`); the sign-in page offers **Sign in with** the provider's name (`login_sso`, `login_sso_callback`). Administrators remove a link with the signed account action `remove_single_sign_on`; **Force password reset** (`reset_password`) and two-factor resets (the account action and the `reset_two_factor` command) now also remove the account's link.
  > - `sign_in_factors` can be `["identity_provider"]` or `["identity_provider", <second factor>]`. Account audit values gain `single_sign_on` (the linked issuer, subject and label, or null); new audit actions `account.single_sign_on_linked`, `account.single_sign_on_unlinked` and `account.remove_single_sign_on`. New table `accounts.SingleSignOnLink` (migration `accounts.0009_single_sign_on_link`). The sign-in log gains `signin.single_sign_on_failed`. New dependencies `authlib` (with `joserfc`) and `requests` (with `urllib3`, `idna`, `charset-normalizer` and `certifi`).

- **Added**: Stability pulls tested in the system against the protocol's acceptance criteria · Stability · 2026-11-16 · [#32](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/32)

  **Assign tests** on a recorded pull creates the tests of its time point, which are recorded, reviewed and investigated like release tests. **Accept pull** records whether the reviewed results meet the acceptance criteria, and the study page shows the results of each storage condition by time point beside the criteria.

  In the application: **Stability pulls**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Stability testing in the system: a stability protocol names the specification that states its acceptance criteria, and its approval is refused while that specification's version in force cannot answer a test of the protocol. **Assign tests** on a recorded pull creates the tests of its time point, each freezing the criterion in force; they are recorded, reviewed, batched and investigated like release tests and belong to the pull, so the record of the study's lot, released or not, does not change. A failing result opens an investigation that holds the pull; a retest of the material pulled can be authorized, a resample cannot. **Accept pull** records whether the reviewed results meet the acceptance criteria and freezes them with the signature; a confirmed failure is accepted with the outcome that they were not met. The study page shows the results of each storage condition by time point beside the criteria, and the stability overview counts pulls outside the acceptance criteria. **Assign tests** refuses criteria approved after the page was opened. A study is not closed while testing of its pulls is in progress.
  > - A test belongs to a lot or to a stability pull. `AnalyticalTest.lot` and `.sample`, and `Investigation.lot`, are empty for a test of a pull, which has `pull` instead; a deployment that reads tests or investigations must accept both. Testing asks the class named by the new setting `ANALYTICAL_STABILITY_PULLS` (`requirements`, `refusal`, `lock`) about pulls; without it no pull is tested in the system.
  > - A stability pull with its own tests takes no linked sample or external evidence, and the pull page shows **Link evidence** only while it has none. Accepting a pull also refuses whoever produced data for, or investigated, one of its tests.

- **Added**: Two-factor sign-in with an authenticator app and recovery codes · Account access · 2026-11-16 · [#34](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/34)

  An owner can set up an authenticator app on **Two-factor sign-in** and then signs in with the password and a current code. Ten one-time recovery codes are shown once, and wrong codes count toward the account's sign-in lock.

  In the application: **Two-factor sign-in**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Two-factor sign-in. **Two-factor sign-in** (`/accounts/two-factor/`, linked from Account access) sets up an authenticator app: confirm the password, scan the QR code or type the key, and confirm with a code from the app; ten one-time recovery codes are then shown once. An account with an authenticator signs in in two steps: the password, then a current code or an unused recovery code on `/accounts/login/verify/` within five minutes (`MFA_PENDING_SECONDS`). Each code from the app works once; wrong codes count toward the account's sign-in failure limit and lock (`LOGIN_FAILURE_LIMIT`, `LOGIN_LOCK_SECONDS`), and 100 consecutive wrong codes stop the second factor until an administrator resets it. New recovery codes, a new app or turning it off need the password and a current code.
  > - New audit actions: `account.two_factor_enabled`, `account.two_factor_replaced`, `account.two_factor_disabled`, `account.two_factor_stopped`, `account.recovery_codes_replaced`, `account.recovery_code_used` and `account.reset_two_factor`. The sign-in log adds `signin.second_factor_requested` and `signin.second_factor_failed`.
  > - The `authentication_context` of a web signature gains `sign_in_factors`: `["password"]`, `["password", "totp"]` or `["password", "recovery_code"]`, as the signer's session signed in. Account audit values (`before`/`after` of `account.*` events) gain `two_factor`, `two_factor_stopped` and `recovery_codes_left`. `LoginThrottle` gains `code_failures`.
  > - New dependencies: `django-otp` (time-based codes and the authenticator model, apps `django_otp` and `django_otp.plugins.otp_totp`) and `segno` (the QR code). The library's per-device delay is off (`OTP_TOTP_THROTTLE_FACTOR = 0`): failed codes count toward the account's own sign-in lock instead. Its admin page for authenticators is not registered.
  > - `accounts.authentication.confirm_password` takes `reset=False` to leave the failure count alone after a correct password, for a check that continues with a second factor; for an account with two-factor sign-in it never resets the count, so changing the password or the PIN cannot clear failures between guessed codes.

- **Changed**: Approving a version retires the earlier version it overlaps · Rule sets · 2026-11-15 · [#29](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/29)

  Approving a version of a rule set, specification, method or sampling plan whose effective period overlaps an approved version no longer fails. The earlier version is retired and keeps its approved content and signature, and the approval page lists what the signature retires. A lot on a retired version needs its requirements assigned or replaced before tests are assigned or it is dispositioned.

  In the application: **Rule sets**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Approving a version of a rule set, specification, method or sampling plan whose effective period overlaps an approved version is no longer refused with "Effective dates overlap an approved version." The earlier version is retired instead: it stops applying from the new version's start, or from the moment of approval if that start has passed, and keeps its approved content and signature. The approval page lists what the signature retires. A draft that would retire a later-numbered approved version is refused.
  > - A lot on a rule version that has been retired cannot have tests assigned or be dispositioned until its requirements are assigned again (before testing) or replaced (during testing) under the version in force. Assigning requirements before testing now moves the lot to the version in force of its own rule set.
  > - Reviewing a result no longer requires the lot's rule version to be in force, only approved, so a result awaiting review and an open investigation are not stranded when a later rule version is approved. Assigning tests and the disposition still require it.
  > - The new-lot form offers only the rule versions in force.
  > - **New QC batch** also offers an earlier revision of a method while open tests not yet in a batch are frozen to it; before, such tests could not get a batch once their method revision was no longer in force. `create_batch` takes an optional `revision`.

- **Added**: Rely on a supplier's result in place of a test under a signed qualification · Suppliers · 2026-11-15 · [#28](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/28)

  Quality records a supplier qualification for a supplier, a material and named tests, and a second quality person signs it. Where the lot's rule set allows it, a result on the supplier's certificate can be proposed and then accepted in place of the laboratory's test with a signature.

  In the application: **Suppliers**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Reliance on a supplier's results: quality records a supplier qualification for one supplier, one material and named tests, with how the supplier's results were confirmed, an evidence reference and validity dates; a second quality person signs it and quality can revoke it. Where the lot's rule set allows it, an analyst proposes a result stated on the lot's current supplier certificate in place of the laboratory's test and a reviewer who neither proposed it nor recorded the certificate or the receipt details signs the acceptance. The proposal is refused unless a signed qualification covers the supplier, the material, the test and the day the lot was received, the certificate states the method and the limits, the stated result meets the specification, no other certificate of the lot contradicts it and the laboratory has not started testing the requirement (a result, a raw-data file, a QC batch or a decision); a refusal by the rule set or for want of a qualification is audited. An accepted result answers its requirement for the whole lot, is listed apart from the laboratory's own results where the disposition is signed and on the certificate of analysis, and can be withdrawn while the lot is in quarantine: a proposal with a reason, a signed acceptance with a signature. An acceptance stops standing, and blocks the disposition, when the certificate record, the receipt's supplier or date, or the requirement it relied on changes. No preset allows reliance, and the software does not decide which tests are identity tests or how often a supplier is confirmed again.
  > - A rule set policy may carry the optional key `supplier_results` with `own_tests`, the list of test codes the laboratory always performs itself. A rule set without it allows no reliance on supplier results; rule sets approved earlier stay valid unchanged.
  > - The testing gate asks the class named by the new setting `ANALYTICAL_SUPPLIER_RESULTS` (`lot`, `standing`, `standing_by_lot`) which supplier results were accepted in place of tests. A deployment that replaced the testing adapters must provide it; without the setting no supplier result answers a requirement.
  > - A supplier certificate result can now count towards QC disposition, but only through a signed acceptance. The lot record, the supplier certificate page and the supplier register say so where they used to say that supplier results never count. The supplier page no longer shows "Not recorded in this register" under Qualification; it lists the supplier's qualifications.
  > - Whoever proposed a supplier's result in place of a test cannot sign that lot's QC disposition. The refusal now reads "You cannot disposition a lot containing your own receipt, supplier certificate, sampling or test data, or a supplier result you proposed in place of a test."
  > - A test whose requirement a supplier's result is proposed or accepted for shows "Not tested · supplier result" and takes no observation, reported result, raw-data file or QC batch until that is withdrawn; no test is assigned for such a requirement.

- **Added**: Replace a lot's requirements during testing with a signature · Lots · 2026-11-15 · [#29](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/29)

  When a specification, a method or the rule set has been revised, a quality person who authored none of the lot's data reviews what the versions in force would change and signs the replacement with a reason. Tests with the same requirement carry over; the others are kept as recorded, marked superseded and never counted.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Controlled replacement of a lot's requirements during testing: when a specification, a method or the rule set has been revised, a quality person who authored none of the lot's data reviews what the versions in force would change and signs the replacement with a reason. Tests whose requirement is exactly the same carry over. The others are kept as recorded, marked superseded and never counted; assigning the lot's tests again adds a linked repeat under the new requirement. The earlier requirements stay in the record, the sampling plan is kept, and the lot moves to the version in force of its rule set. A replacement is refused while an investigation is open on the lot or while a test that would be superseded holds results or raw-data files that were not submitted. Migrations `core.0006`, `catalog.0006`, `sampling.0004`, `analytical.0007` and `quality.0011` add the columns and replace the database guards; they change no existing row.
  > - Once testing has started, assigning a lot's requirements again is refused with "Testing has started on this lot, so its requirements cannot be assigned again. Quality can replace them with a signature."
  > - The testing gate matches a test to a requirement by what the requirement asks for, not by the document that states it, so a test carries over when a lot's requirements are replaced by identical ones.
  > - Tests have a new state, Superseded, and a new kind, Repeat under replaced requirements. A deployment that reads test states or kinds must handle both.
  > - `core.services.sign_transition` takes an optional `prepare` step that runs after the signer is locked and before the signed record is.
  > - Replacing a lot's requirements during testing asks the class named by the new setting `REQUIREMENT_REPLACEMENT_TESTING` (`effects`, `lock`, `apply`) what happens to the lot's tests. Without the setting requirements cannot be replaced once testing has started.

- **Added**: Results reported by contract laboratories under a signed approval · Laboratory · 2026-11-15 · [#27](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/27)

  Quality keeps a register of contract laboratories and approves each laboratory for the methods it may perform, with a second quality person signing. An analyst records what the laboratory's report states for a test, and the result follows the usual review, disposition and certificate path.

  In the application: **Contract laboratories**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Results from contract laboratories: quality keeps a register of contract laboratories and, for each method a laboratory may perform, an approval with an evidence reference and validity dates that a second quality person signs and that can be revoked. An analyst records what the laboratory's report states for a test (the laboratory, the report number and date, where the report is kept and every replicate). The entry is refused unless an approval covers the date of the report, and the approval relied on is kept with the result. The result then follows the usual path: independent review, investigation of a failing result, QC disposition and the certificate of analysis, which names the laboratory and its report. The laboratory's and the approval's pages list the results that relied on them.
  > - A bench class named by `ANALYTICAL_BENCH` now also answers for contract laboratories (`contract_choices`, `authorize_contract`, `record_contract_refusal`, `contract_notice`). A deployment that replaced the bench must add them.
  > - A test that holds a result reported by a contract laboratory can be submitted and reviewed without a QC batch, and its replicates are corrected together from **Correct contract laboratory result**.

- **Added**: Several sets of requirements on one lot · Specifications · 2026-11-15 · [#30](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/30)

  A lot's requirements can be assigned under more than one scope (`general` and named market or customer overlays), and the approved specification of each scope applies in full. A rule set can name the materials, stages or scopes it applies to besides the lot's own. **Assign requirements** takes **Scopes**, separated by commas.

  In the application: **Specifications and methods: Specifications**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Several sets of requirements on one lot: a lot's requirements are assigned under one or more scopes (`general` and named market or customer overlays), and the approved specification of each scope applies in full. A rule set whose policy carries the optional key `applies_to` (`materials`, `stages`, `scopes`) applies to every lot it names beside the lot's own rule set. A test the specifications state alike counts once. A named scope with nothing configured, or a rule set that requires a test no applicable specification requires, places the lot on an applicability hold.
  > - **Assign requirements** takes **Scopes** (one or more, separated by commas) where it took one **Scope**. `sampling.services.assign_requirements` accepts `scopes` as well as `scope`, and `catalog.services.resolve_requirements` accepts `scopes` and `decisions`.
  > - A lot assigned under several scopes, or under an additional rule set, freezes a requirement payload with the schema `oq.requirements/2`: the keys of `oq.requirements/1` (`specification` is the first specification) and `scopes`, `specifications`, `additional_rules`, `decisions` and, on each test, the `sources` that state it. A lot under one scope and its own rule set keeps `oq.requirements/1` unchanged. A deployment that reads the payload must accept both.
  > - A rule set whose policy states `applies_to` is not offered when a lot is received and is refused by `receive_lot`. A rule set cannot gain or lose `applies_to` from one version to the next.
  > - Assigning tests and the disposition require every rule set version the lot is under to be in force, the additional ones included, and a supplier's result is relied on only when each of them allows it. A requirement provider named by `ANALYTICAL_REQUIREMENT_PROVIDER` may offer `require_additional_rules(lot)`; a provider without it applies no additional rule set.
  > - The rule set approval page counts, for a version being retired, the quarantined lots whose requirements apply it as an additional rule set as well as the lots received under it.
  > - The database constraint `lot_assignment_replacement` is replaced by `lot_assignment_origin`, and `sampling_lotassignment` gains the columns `scopes` and `decision`.
  > - The specification form and page no longer say that overlays are never applied together: a lot is assigned under every scope it falls under.
  > - The native evidence of a certificate lists `scopes`, `specifications`, `additional_rules` and `decisions` for a lot that has them; evidence of a lot under one specification keeps its shape.
  > - Assigning a lot's requirements locks the account before the lot, like every other change to a lot.

- **Added**: Signed decision where the requirements that apply to a lot differ · Lots · 2026-11-15 · [#30](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/30)

  Where the specifications that apply to a lot state a test differently, nothing is merged and neither statement is picked. A quality person who authored none of the lot's data chooses which requirement applies, gives a reason and signs under **Decide conflicting requirements**.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - A signed decision where the specifications that apply to a lot state a test differently: nothing is merged and neither statement is picked. A quality person who authored none of the lot's data chooses which requirement applies, gives a reason and signs (meaning `requirements_decided`, page **Decide conflicting requirements**); the statements not chosen stay in the record, on the disposition page and on the certificate. During testing the same choice is part of the signed replacement of the lot's requirements.
  > - The evidence of a replacement (`oq.requirement-replacement/1`) gains `versions` (every specification and additional rule set version that changed), and `decisions` with `signed_at` when a choice between differing statements is part of it. Earlier rows are unchanged and are read as before.

- **Added**: Receipt details on each lot and a register of suppliers · Suppliers · 2026-11-14 · [#24](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/24)

  A lot is received together with where it came from, the supplier's and manufacturer's lot numbers, the delivery document, the quantity, the containers and what the examination on receipt found. Quality keeps a register of suppliers under **Suppliers**, and the lot list shows the supplier and searches both lot numbers.

  In the application: **Suppliers**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Receipt details and a supplier register: a lot is received together with where it came from (a supplier from the register, or made on site), the supplier's and manufacturer's lot numbers, the delivery document, the date, the quantity, the containers and what the examination on receipt found. Details are never edited; a correction adds a linked record with its reason while the lot is in quarantine. Quality keeps the register, which records identity only and does not qualify a supplier. The lot list shows the supplier and searches supplier and manufacturer lot numbers. Lots received earlier have no receipt details until an analyst records them.
  > - Whoever recorded or corrected a lot's receipt details can no longer sign that lot's QC disposition. The **Number** field of the new-lot form is now **Lot number**.

- **Added**: Record a supplier's certificate of analysis on a lot · Lots · 2026-11-14 · [#26](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/26)

  For a quarantined lot received from a supplier, an analyst records what the supplier's certificate states, and each result is shown against the lot's requirement. These are the supplier's results: they are kept apart from the laboratory's own tests.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Supplier certificates: for a quarantined lot received from a supplier, an analyst records what the supplier's certificate of analysis states (its number, issuer, date and printed lot number, where it is kept, and for each of the lot's approved requirements the result, method and limits as stated). Each result is compared with the lot's requirement and shown as meeting it or not. These are the supplier's results: they answer no requirement, are not part of the disposition evidence and are not printed on the certificate of analysis. A result that does not meet the specification is shown on the lot record and on the disposition page and does not hold the lot. A correction adds a linked record; a record made in error is withdrawn and kept.
  > - Whoever recorded, corrected or withdrew a supplier certificate of a lot cannot sign that lot's QC disposition.

- **Added**: Attach raw-data files to a test · Testing · 2026-11-13 · [#22](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/22)

  A raw-data file can be attached to a test. It is stored with its SHA-256 checksum, never changes and is returned unchanged on download.

  In the application: **Testing: tests**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Raw-data files: a file can be attached to a test, is stored with its SHA-256 checksum, never changes and is returned unchanged on download. `RAW_DATA_MAX_BYTES` sets the largest accepted file and `RAW_DATA_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES` an optional ceiling for all files together. A larger file is refused in the browser before it is sent, and the server answers an oversized upload with status 413 without reading it.

- **Added**: Equipment, reagent and analyst checks when a result is entered · Testing · 2026-11-13 · [#22](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/22)

  Recording or correcting a result, or a batch QC check, names the instruments and the reagent or standard lots used, and is refused when one of them is not fit for use or the analyst has no current qualification for the method. After a failed calibration the equipment page lists the tests and QC batches that used the equipment.

  In the application: **Equipment**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Equipment and reagent checks at result entry: recording or correcting a result or a batch QC check names the instruments and the reagent or standard lots used. An entry is refused when an instrument is out of service or out of calibration, a lot is not released or expired, or the analyst has no current qualification for the method, which now applies to batch QC as well. A method version can require an instrument, a lot or both. After a failed calibration the equipment page lists the tests and QC batches that used the equipment.
  > - `ANALYTICAL_BENCH` replaces `ANALYTICAL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK`. A deployment that overrides the old setting must name a bench class instead; without one, results are held.

- **Security**: Oversized uploads are refused before the request is read · Whole application · 2026-11-13 · [#23](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/23)

  A file above the raw-data size limit is refused in the browser when it is chosen, and the server answers an oversized upload with status 413 without reading it. Before, a slow oversized upload kept a server process busy until it had arrived, and it needed no account.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > `core.uploads.UploadSizeMiddleware` is listed ahead of the CSRF check, the first code that reads a submitted form. A multipart request that declares more than `RAW_DATA_MAX_BYTES` plus 1 MiB (room for the form's other fields) gets status 413 and a short page (`templates/413.html`), and its body is left unread. The margin is a constant, not a setting. A file over the limit inside the margin is still stopped by the upload handler and the page returns with the same message as before.
  >
  > The answer is given before the view runs, so sign-in, role and test-state checks do not apply to it; it changes nothing and shows only the size limit. It relies on the server closing the connection after the answer: Gunicorn's default worker does and reads at most 64 KiB more. A different server, or a proxy that buffers uploads, may still receive the whole request (`docs/operations.md`). No migration and no new setting.

- **Added**: Results calculated from a method's formula · Testing · 2026-11-13 · [#22](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/22)

  A method version can define one formula over named inputs with units. The analyst enters the inputs, the system calculates the result, and the result keeps the inputs, the formula and the method version.

  In the application: **Specifications and methods: Methods**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Calculated results: a method version can define one formula over named inputs with units, approved and frozen with the version. The analyst enters the inputs, the system calculates the value, and the result keeps the inputs, the formula and the method version. Submission and review calculate again.

- **Added**: Count, qualitative and less-than results, and limits that exclude their boundary · Testing · 2026-11-12 · [#21](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/21)

  Native testing records counts, qualitative results (conforms or does not conform, absent or present) with what was observed, and results reported as less than a value. Specification limits can exclude their boundary, and certificates show the acceptance text and the result as recorded.

  In the application: **Testing: tests**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - More result types in native testing: counts, qualitative results (conforms or does not conform, absent or present) recorded with what was observed, results reported as less than a value kept as recorded, and specification limits that exclude their boundary. Certificates show the acceptance text and the result as recorded. A qualitative specification line now needs an expected outcome; lines approved without one are held until a new version states it.
  >
  > Count result type and `expected_result` on specification lines; `oq.test-requirement/2` for the new shapes. Readings carry a qualifier, outcome and observed text; the reportable text is frozen at submission and checked again at review. A less-than result never becomes zero and never enters a mean.

- **Added**: First public source release · Whole application · 2026-11-10

  OpenBGA QM LIMS is published as source under AGPL-3.0-only. It covers approved methods and specifications, sampling, lot and sample records, results with replicates, investigations, independent review and QC disposition, certificates of analysis, laboratory resources, stability, signatures, the audit trail and named user accounts.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > Initial public source release (project version 0.1.0), licensed AGPL-3.0-only. Implemented areas:
  >
  > - Approved methods and specifications, sampling plans and sampling assignments, with independently approved revisions and frozen applicability snapshots on lot assignments.
  > - Lot and sample records, numeric observations with replicates, and method QC batches.
  > - Out-of-specification investigations with controlled assessment, retest and resample authorization, and conclusion.
  > - Independent signed review and QC disposition that checks assigned requirements, review state, investigations, independence and active holds.
  > - Immutable PDF certificates of analysis with signed issuance, amendments, stored bytes, snapshots and checksums.
  > - Laboratory resource records and method-specific analyst qualification authorization.
  > - Stability protocols and scheduled pulls, reserves, retention obligations and holds.
  > - Shared rule revisions, PIN signatures (hashed, rate-limited, re-entered for every signing) and attributed audit history.
  > - Named user accounts with explicit roles, signed account administration, session limits and a read-only Django admin.
  > - In-app page documentation for every staff page, and a static presentation website published with GitHub Pages.
  > - Sign-in throttling, a same-origin Content-Security-Policy and credential masking in error reports.
  > - Container image, CI workflow, a Docker Compose profile for local evaluation and a Render Blueprint for manual deployment.
  >
  > Limits at the first release:
  >
  > - Greater-than results and batch QC checks other than directly entered numeric values with inclusive limits are not supported. A method states that an instrument or a lot is required, not which one.
  > - Stability testing compares each result with its acceptance criterion. Trend rules, a significant change from the initial value, shelf-life evaluation, a hold on the lot after a failing result and reports to authorities are left to the laboratory.
  > - Manufacturer batch release is a separate decision and is not performed by the software.
  > - Multi-factor authentication, identity proofing, PIN recovery policy, backup schedules and storage, restore acceptance, retention and intended-use validation remain the responsibility of each deployment.
  > - Segment presets are synthetic drafts, not complete policies.
  > - No regulatory compliance, validation or certification is claimed. Use synthetic data only.

### Medium impact

- **Added**: Certificates carry their data in a machine-readable form, inside a tagged PDF/A-3a file · Certificates · 2026-11-18 · [#56](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/56)

  Each certificate issued or amended now holds its content as a JSON file, attached to the PDF and downloadable beside it with **Download data** on the version and certificate pages, where its checksum is shown. The PDF is written for long-term keeping and for assistive technology (tagged PDF/A-3a, also declaring PDF/UA-1). A certificate for one customer or market carries that scope only, and certificates issued before stay exactly as issued, without data.

  In the application: **Certificates of analysis**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Migration `reporting.0005_certificate_data`: `ReportVersion.data` (the JSON bytes, null for versions issued before), `data_sha256` and `pdf_format` (`PDF/A-3a, PDF/UA-1`), guarded like every issued column, with the check constraint `reportversion_data`.
  > - Schema `oq.certificate-data/1`, described in `docs/certificate-data.md`; the PDF attaches it as `certificate-data.json` with `AFRelationship /Data`.
  > - New download `reports/<id>/versions/<n>/data/` (URL name `reporting:data`), checked against its checksum and audited as `report.data_downloaded`.
  > - The lot record export adds `files/certificates/<number>-v<n>-data.json` and the check `certificate data file`; `verify_restore` checks the data checksum with the certificates.

- **Changed**: A test record offers New QC batch when no open batch accepts the test · Testing · 2026-11-17

  **Add to QC batch** is offered only when an open QC batch of the test's method revision accepts it. Otherwise the header says why and offers **New QC batch**, which opens with that method revision already chosen.

  In the application: **Testing: tests**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > `analytical.views.batch_offer` is shared by the test record and the Add to QC batch page; `batch_new` reads `?method=<code>&revision=<n>`.

- **Changed**: Certificate of analysis and lot record PDFs use the new design · Certificates · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  The certificate of analysis and the exported lot record share one print layout that stays readable in black and white. Every regulated element is kept, and no new sentence is printed on the certificate. Certificates already issued are stored files and keep their original bytes.

  In the application: **Certificates of analysis**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > Both PDFs share one print stylesheet. A test downloads a certificate issued before the change and compares it byte for byte with the stored copy; 64 certificate elements were checked against the checklist. The renderer (`reporting/render.py`) loads only the vendored font and status glyphs, by exact URL, through a fetcher allowlist.

- **Added**: Dashboard shows the QC flow with counts · Dashboard · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  The **Dashboard** shows the QC flow from lot to sample, result, review, disposition and certificate of analysis, with the number of items waiting at each stage and the date of the oldest. Each count opens the list it counts.

  In the application: **Dashboard**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > `quality/dashboard.py`. Every queue is one aggregate query (count and oldest date) on the same conditions as the list it links to, so a count and its list agree. Counts are not scoped per user: every reader role sees the same laboratory, as in the lists, and the services decide who may act. A lot can sit in two queues; a stage total is the sum of its queues.

- **Changed**: Every dashboard and overview count opens exactly the items it counts · Dashboard · 2026-11-17

  Each count on the **Dashboard**, the **Stability** overview and the **Laboratory** overview now opens a list that shows exactly that many rows, and every Dashboard queue is a link. **Material lots** has a new **Queue** filter for the Dashboard's lot queues, **Sampling** a status **Awaiting quality assessment**, **Testing** a status **Retests and resamples not done**, and **Reserve samples** a status **Retention anchor not yet known**.

  In the application: **Dashboard**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Lot queues are defined once in `quality.dashboard.LOT_QUEUES` / `lot_queues()`; the material lot list filters by the same querysets (`?queue=<key>`).
