Test queues use `analytical.views.TEST_FILTERS` (new key `repeats`); sampling deviations use `sampling.views.deviation_to_assess()`; reserves use `stability.views._reserve_filter`.
  > - Tests open, Awaiting review and open investigations now include stability testing, as their lists do. Queues that open a list of lots count lots.
  > - `tests/test_dashboard.py` and the overview tests compare every linked count with the rows of its list for each reader role.

- **Added**: Every page's help starts with a summary and the common tasks · Page help · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  The page-help panel opens with a short summary of the page, the common tasks with the exact labels to use and a few things worth knowing, above the full reference. Every staff page has it.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > 182 pages carry the friendly layer in the redesigned drawer, and the page-documentation coverage test requires it for every page.

- **Added**: Filter the lot list by status · Lots · 2026-11-17 · [#44](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/44)

  The material lot list has a **Status** filter, and the lot record shows a rejection or cancellation with its signer, grounds, reason and reference.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - The material lot list has a **Status** filter (Quarantine, Released, Rejected, Cancelled), and the lot record shows a rejection or cancellation with its signer, grounds, reason and reference.

- **Changed**: Investigations account for tests recorded as not completed · Testing · 2026-11-17 · [#45](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/45)

  A retest or resample recorded as not completed before it held any reading no longer uses up the investigation's retest allowance. An investigation can still be concluded when the test opened for it was recorded as not completed.

  In the application: **Testing: investigations**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - The retest allowance of an investigation (`retests_used`) no longer counts an authorized retest or resample recorded as not completed before it held any reading, correction or raw-data file. An investigation is not concluded as invalidated while one of its tests was recorded as not completed with a reading outside the limits, and the investigation opened on a test recorded as not completed can be concluded although that test was never reviewed.

- **Added**: List columns, page size, sort and sidebar state are saved for each user · Whole application · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  Every list remembers the page size, sort order and columns a person chose, and the sidebar and the page-help panel remember whether they are collapsed or open. The settings follow the account, so they apply on a shared laboratory workstation after sign-in. Lists hide low-priority columns by their own width so they fit 1280 and 1440 pixel screens and an open help panel.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > Stored on the server in `core.UserPreference` (migration `core/0007_user_preference.py`). The endpoint is `/preferences/` (per user, CSRF-protected) with `core.preferences.GridPreferenceMiddleware`; the page-help panel keeps its own state in the same table. Writes that arrive out of order no longer overwrite a later one.

- **Added**: Lot record lists the lot's retention obligations · Lots · 2026-11-17

  The lot record shows a **Retention** panel when the lot has retention obligations, including those recorded for the lot without a reserve sample: the basis, the anchor or **Anchor not yet known**, the date it is retained through and the reserve sample. Analysts and quality users can **Set anchor** there while the anchor is unknown.

  In the application: **Material lots**

- **Fixed**: New QC batch no longer fails when no batch method is approved · Testing · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  **New QC batch** returned an error page when there was no approved batch method. It now opens with the notice "No approved batch method is available; batches are held."

  In the application: **Testing: QC batches**

- **Changed**: Password and Sign-in announcement pages show the current state · Account access · 2026-11-17

  **Password** now shows whether a new password is required and when you last changed it; **Change password** opens the change in a dialog. **Sign-in announcement** shows the notice as visitors see it and its history; **Change announcement** opens the signed change. Account changes and the announcement change are signed on the same signature card as other signing pages.

  In the application: **Password**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > New URL names `accounts:password` (`/accounts/password/`) and `accounts:announcement_change` (`/accounts/announcement/change/`); `accounts:password_change` moved to `/accounts/password/change/`. A required password change still goes straight to the change form.

- **Fixed**: Pulls of a terminated study are no longer shown as overdue or due · Stability · 2026-11-17

  A pull that was not taken or not accepted when its study was terminated now reads **Terminated** and no longer counts as **Overdue**, **Due now**, **Upcoming** or **Awaiting acceptance** in the pull list, on the study page, in the Stability overview or on the Dashboard. **Mark missed** is no longer offered for it.

  In the application: **Stability pulls**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > `stability.views._pull_filter` limits the work statuses to active studies; the overview and the Dashboard count through it. A closed study and its pulls already took no more work (`stability.services.close_study`).

- **Fixed**: Record pages offer only the actions the server would accept now · Whole application · 2026-11-17

  A record page no longer offers an action that would only lead to a refusal. Where an action that would be offered cannot be taken now, the page header says why instead, for example on an investigation (**Authorize retest**, **Conclude**), a test (**Sign review**, **Return test**, **Record not completed**, **Record contract laboratory result**), a lot (**Reject lot**, **Cancel lot received in error**, **Review disposition**, **Replace requirements**), a draft version (**Review and approve**), equipment (**Return to service**), a stability protocol or study (**Approve**, **Close study**) and an intended use (**Accept**).

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > Each page computes the same refusal its action page and service check (for example `services.authorize_refusal`, `services.review_refusal`, `quality.rejection.rejection_refusals`, `catalog.web.approval_offer`, `stability.views.close_refusal`, `validation.views.accept_denial`); the services still recheck everything under lock. Ops record pages show a refusal with `laboratory.ui.refused`.

- **Changed**: Selects, dates, files and plain create forms use shared controls · Whole application · 2026-11-17 · [#46](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/46)

  Selects, date and date-time fields, file fields and decimal inputs with units look and behave the same on every page, and a select that searches records shows only what the person may use. Plain create forms open in a dialog that asks before unsaved changes are lost; signing pages never use the dialog.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Tom Select replaces every browser select. A permission-scoped remote select is served by `core/lookups.py` (one endpoint, `/lookups/<name>/`, and a registry; role-scoped querysets, `tests/test_lookups.py`).
  > - A shared date and date-time popover (week starting Sunday, Today, Yesterday, Now and Clear; laboratory-local time), decimals kept as typed with unit addons, a file drop zone and tooltips. All forms are `novalidate` with server errors shown inline.
  > - Form dialog: `core.form_dialog.FormDialogMiddleware` and the context processor `core.form_surfaces.form_presentation`; the sticky footer is only in dialogs and a record's history is never inside one.

- **Changed**: Stability no longer accepts rejected or cancelled lots · Stability · 2026-11-17 · [#44](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/44)

  A study cannot be started on a rejected or cancelled lot, and a reserve sample, retention obligation or hold is refused on a cancelled lot. Their forms no longer offer those lots.

  In the application: **Stability studies**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Stability refuses to start a study on a rejected or cancelled lot, and refuses a reserve sample, retention obligation or hold on a cancelled lot; their forms no longer offer those lots.

- **Changed**: The validation pack of each commit includes the acceptance journeys' evidence · Deployment · 2026-11-17 · [#49](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/49)

  Every commit's checks now run the acceptance journeys with the application image, and the validation pack built from them includes the evidence the journeys wrote. A failed journey fails the pack.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > CI's container smoke job runs the acceptance journeys with the application image in a new database, and the validation pack includes their evidence under `acceptance/` (`scripts/validation_pack.py build --acceptance DIR`, which checks the folder against its `SHA256SUMS` and refuses a run of another commit); a failed run fails the pack.

- **Changed**: Unsubmitted readings are judged against their limits when a batch or lot is rejected · Testing · 2026-11-17 · [#45](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/45)

  Rejecting a QC batch or a lot now also judges readings that were never submitted. A reading counts as outside its limits when it fails once rounded to the reporting precision, and a batch rejection then opens an investigation.

  In the application: **Testing: QC batches**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Batch rejection and lot rejection judge readings that were never submitted with `outside_limits`: a reading also counts as outside its limits when it fails once rounded half-up to the reporting precision, and a complete replicate set when the result submission would calculate fails; batch rejection then opens an investigation, and lot rejection waits for one. Batch rejection locks the investigations of its tests before the tests, which removes a deadlock with concluding an investigation whose retest was in the batch. Investigation triggers are shortened to fit their 200 characters.

- **Added**: What's new lists every change, with a count of those since you last looked · Whole application · 2026-11-17

  **What's new** at the top right of every page lists the changes to OpenBGA QM LIMS, newest month first and ranked by impact, with what each means for your work and where to find it. A number beside it counts the changes made since you last looked; opening the list clears it for your account on every workstation. A new account starts with no number.

  In the application: **What's new**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - New app `whatsnew` (no models, no migration) and page `whatsnew:index` at `/whats-new/`. Each change is one file in `changelog.d/`, which ships with the application; nothing is fetched over the network.
  > - `CHANGELOG.md` is now generated from `changelog.d/` by `python manage.py changelog`; `--check` fails when an entry is invalid or the file is stale. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` by hand.
  > - The last change a user was shown is the presentation preference `whatsnew.seen`, set by the server the first time a page renders for the user and whenever the list is opened.
  > - The validation pack's `release-notes.md` is the whole generated `CHANGELOG.md` of the commit.

- **Added**: Administrators can reset an account's two-factor sign-in · Users and roles · 2026-11-16 · [#34](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/34)

  An administrator can remove an account's authenticator and recovery codes with a signed **Reset two-factor sign-in**, which also ends its sessions. **Users and roles** shows and filters accounts by two-factor sign-in.

  In the application: **Users and roles**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - **Reset two-factor sign-in** on an account (admin, signed with the meaning `account_authorized`, not on one's own account) removes its authenticator and recovery codes and ends its sessions; the audited command `reset_two_factor <username> --actor <administrator> --reason ...` does the same from the operator shell. **Users and roles** shows and filters accounts by two-factor sign-in.

- **Changed**: Product renamed to OpenBGA QM LIMS · Whole application · 2026-11-16 · [#41](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/41)

  The product is now OpenBGA QM LIMS, with the repository `openbga/qm-lims`. The name appears in the application, certificate and record PDFs, passkey and authenticator-app names, documentation and the presentation. Issued PDFs keep their original bytes.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Renamed the product to **OpenBGA QM LIMS** and the repository to `openbga/qm-lims` (the former `openbga/fresh-coa-lims` address redirects): application name, titles, top bar, footer, certificate and record PDFs, passkey and authenticator-app names, README, documentation, presentation and project links. The presentation moves to <https://openbga.github.io/qm-lims/> (the old address no longer serves it). The Python package is `openbga-qm-lims`, backup file names in the runbook start with `qm-lims-`, and the CI image tag is `qm-lims:ci`. Unchanged on purpose: the database name and user `open_qual`, the Render resources `fresh-coa-lims`, `fresh-coa-lims-db` and `fresh-coa-lims-demo-reset` and the demo at `fresh-coa-lims.onrender.com`, the backup manifest and restore report format identifiers (`fresh-coa-lims.backup-manifest/1`, `fresh-coa-lims.restore-check/1`, so existing backups still verify) and the `freshcoa-pagedocs-*` browser storage keys. Issued PDFs keep their original bytes.

- **Added**: Validation pack built with each release · Deployment · 2026-11-16 · [#38](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/38)

  Each release can build a pack that traces every product requirement to the tests that give evidence for it, with each suite's results and the environment. It is supplier evidence for a laboratory's own validation, not a validation of the system.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Validation pack of each release. `docs/traceability.toml` traces every product requirement of `docs/product.md` to the tests that give evidence for it, and `tests/test_validation_pack.py` refuses a requirement without a test, an entry that does not exist or a test that is not traced. `scripts/validation_pack.py` (`check`, `environment`, `build`) builds the pack: `index.html`, `requirements.csv`, `traceability.csv`, `pack.json`, each suite's JUnit results and environment, the requirements, regulatory matrix and map of the commit, the release notes and `SHA256SUMS`. Each suite's conftest writes the commit the tests run on into the JUnit file, and `[skips]` in the map names the tests that may be skipped, with the reason. CI's application and browser jobs write their JUnit results, and a new `validation-pack` job builds the pack after both and the container smoke job pass and keeps it as the artifact `validation-pack-<commit>` for 90 days. The pack is supplier evidence for a laboratory's own validation, not a validation of the system.

- **Added**: Withdraw a draft stability protocol · Stability · 2026-11-16 · [#32](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/32)

  The author or a quality person can withdraw a draft protocol that will not be approved, with a reason, and the next version of its code can then be drafted. Protocols have a new state, Withdrawn.

  In the application: **Stability protocols**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - **Withdraw draft** on a draft stability protocol: its author or a quality person withdraws a draft that will not be approved, with a reason, and the next version of the code can then be drafted. Protocols have a new state, Withdrawn.

- **Fixed**: Assigning requirements again keeps the sampling plan of earlier samples · Sampling · 2026-11-15 · [#29](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/29)

  Assigning a lot's requirements again after it was sampled keeps the sampling plan version its samples were taken under. Before, a plan version approved in between left the earlier samples blocking the lot with no way to clear them.

  In the application: **Sampling: Lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Assigning a lot's requirements again after it was sampled keeps the sampling plan version its samples were taken under. Before, a plan version approved in between left the earlier samples blocking the lot with no way to clear them.

- **Fixed**: Requirement replacement can be signed again after a refused signature · Lots · 2026-11-15 · [#30](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/30)

  After a refused signature the replacement page can be signed after review without being opened again. Before, every further attempt was refused as stale.

  In the application: **Material lots**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - After a refused signature the replacement page carries the token and the lot revision of what it then shows, so it can be signed after review without being opened again; before, every further attempt was refused as stale.

- **Added**: Hosted demonstration is reset daily and its shared accounts are locked · Deployment · 2026-11-12 · [#19](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/19)

  The hosted demonstration can be returned to a known state every day. The password and PIN of a published demonstration account can no longer be changed by whoever signs in with it, so one visitor cannot lock out the others.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > `reset_demo` (new command) empties every application table, creates `demo_admin` with its own private password and PIN, runs `seed_demo` and, with `--publish-accounts`, locks the listed accounts and publishes the announcement, signed by `demo_admin`.
  >
  > - Refused before anything is erased: `ALLOW_DEMO_RESET=true` is not set (`DEBUG` alone is not enough); one of the four credentials is missing, malformed or shared between `demo_admin` and the published pair; the schema is not this release's; the database has accounts but not the seed's `demo_admin`; `--journey` outside `DEBUG`.
  > - Credential lock: `User.credentials_locked` (migration `accounts.0006`). The services refuse a change of password or PIN of a locked account and the two pages explain it instead of showing the form. An administrator's forced password reset or PIN re-enrollment ends the lock.
  > - `seed_demo` also runs without `DEBUG` where `ALLOW_DEMO_RESET=true` is set, refuses `--journey` outside `DEBUG`, says what each account is for in the announcement and can end it with `DEMO_RESET_NOTE`.
  > - `render.demo.yaml` is a separate Blueprint with one cron job, every day at 08:00 UTC. It creates nothing until it is created by hand (`docs/operations.md`, "Demonstration reset").
  > - The reset is not one transaction (signing refuses to run inside an enclosing transaction): the erase, the accounts and the draft configuration commit together and the signed steps follow. The whole-table erase bypasses the history triggers on purpose, which is why the command is fenced by the opt-in and the demonstration-database check. The first run erases accounts created by hand.

- **Changed**: Product renamed to OpenBGA Fresh CoA LIMS with a new mark · Whole application · 2026-11-12 · [#7](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/7)

  The application, newly issued certificates, documentation and the presentation use the name OpenBGA Fresh CoA LIMS and a certificate-and-leaf mark. Certificates issued earlier keep their original bytes.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Adopted the OpenBGA Fresh CoA LIMS name and certificate-and-leaf mark across the application, presentation and newly issued certificates.
  >
  > No database migration and no dependency version change. The product has since been renamed again (see the entry for OpenBGA QM LIMS).

- **Added**: Publish a notice on the sign-in page with a signed change · Sign-in announcement · 2026-11-12 · [#17](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/17)

  Administrators write, publish and withdraw one notice that is shown on the sign-in page. Each change needs a reason and a PIN signature and is kept in the audit trail. It is found under **Sign-in announcement** for the administrator role.

  In the application: **Sign-in announcement**

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - Sign-in announcement: one notice on the sign-in page that administrators write, publish and withdraw with a signed, audited change. The development seed can publish its non-administrator demo accounts there (`seed_demo --publish-accounts`).
  >
  > Migration `accounts.0005_login_announcement` adds one table. Each change is signed with the meaning `announcement_authorized`, rechecks the reviewed revision and keeps the previous and new text in the audit trail. The text is escaped and then rendered with the page-documentation subset. `seed_demo --publish-accounts` lists the seeded non-administrator accounts with their shared password and PIN in the announcement, signed by `demo_admin`; it refuses to publish a credential that any administrator or superuser accepts and never replaces text an administrator saved.

- **Added**: Sign-in, failed sign-in and sign-out events are written to the log · Sign-in · 2026-11-12 · [#20](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/20)

  Each sign-in, failed attempt and sign-out leaves one line in the application's log with the event, the username and the request ID. Passwords are never logged.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > Each event writes one `openbga.signin` line to standard output: event, username and the Render `Rndr-Id` request ID. Session expiry or revocation appears as `signout`. The lines live in the platform logs, not in the database, so they survive the demonstration's database resets; the request ID joins the platform's HTTP request log for the client address. A failed attempt names the account only when it exists (`<unknown>` otherwise); a malformed request ID is logged as `-`. Usernames and addresses in these logs are personal data: see the retention table in `docs/operations.md`.

- **Fixed**: The sidebar shows only the pages an account's roles can open · Whole application · 2026-11-12 · [#16](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/16)

  **Audit trail** is no longer offered to analysts and reviewers, who could not open it, and laboratory pages are no longer offered to accounts without a recognized role. Laboratory sections with nothing to show are hidden, and an account with several roles sees the pages of all of them.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > The shared menu is filtered by the account's current explicit roles; read-only laboratory destinations stay available. The audit link and the audit route use the same set of reader roles. Server authorization and scientific action permissions are unchanged. No migration and no dependency change.

- **Changed**: The demonstration deploys develop automatically after checks pass · Deployment · 2026-11-12 · [#17](https://github.com/openbga/qm-lims/pull/17)

  The hosted demonstration is updated from the `develop` branch once the CI checks pass. Controlled deployments are not affected.

  > **Technical notes**
  >
  > - The Render Blueprint and hosted demo now deploy `develop` automatically once CI checks pass; controlled deployments keep automatic deployment off.
  >
